429.canonical: Assign every request a criticality level, provision enough capacity for all critical traffic, and — driven by a task-level utilisation signal such as CPU or memory crossing configured thresholds — shed the lowest-criticality requests first under overload.

441.canonical: Load-test each component to its breaking point in a realistic environment — required for most launches — because a service's overload behaviour cannot be predicted from first principles and you must learn its breaking point and failure mode.

487.canonical: Protect engineers' time in cognitive flow ('the zone') and assign a real cost to interruptions and context switches, because a single short interrupt breaks flow and can cost hours of productive work — so do not treat engineers as freely-interruptible units of work.

530.canonical: Make approved standards, policies, and security assets (libraries, configurations, images, secrets patterns, services) reusable by converting them from static prose into executable blueprints and components in shared repositories and platforms.
